findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this bucket (including an uploaded vendor roster) are not covered by enforced default SSE-KMS encryption.

The bucket declares no ACL and has no associated aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or restrictive bucket policy, so access control falls back to account defaults and a later ACL or policy change could expose report data publicly.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed with no recovery path, permitting undetected data tampering or destruction.
The ledger exports bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial ledger data is stored without enforced default encryption.

Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy = true with no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, so ledger data can be irrecoverably overwritten or deleted and public-access protection is left to account defaults.
No default server-side encryption is configured for the model artifacts bucket, leaving stored artifacts unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose artifacts publicly with no account-level guardrail.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; runbooks commonly contain sensitive procedural and credential-adjacent detail and are stored without enforced encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against future public ACLs or bucket policies.

The audit log destination bucket is created with force_destroy = true and no MFA delete, object lock, or public access block, so the audit record can be deleted wholesale, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.

findings.issue_category: no public access block on log bucket
findings.description: The bucket uses the log-delivery-write ACL and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy, so account-level defaults are the only protection against the access log data being made readable by a later ACL or policy change.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/business-confidential data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so it is stored in cleartext.
Neither this bucket nor any other in the file has a bucket policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests, so objects including the vendor roster may be transmitted in cleartext.
